Xendit is an enterprise payments platform powering complex financial operations across Southeast Asia and global markets. We provide a unified API layer combining payment processing, global payouts, localized FX, identity compliance, and fraud protection. As a trusted financial partner backed by top-tier global investors, Xendit processes high-throughput transaction flows for leading global platforms including Meta, Traveloka, ByteDance, Wise, and Grab, building resilient payment infrastructure to drive regional commerce forward.

Why this role exists

The merchant lifecycle: onboarding, activation, and lifecycle across many surfaces, where consistency and reusability matter as much as any single flow. This role does double duty: raise the craft on the merchant lifecycle experience, and own the design system that keeps that experience coherent as the domain scales. You are the person who both designs the hard flow and builds the pattern that keeps the next ten from drifting.

What you'll own

• Product design in the Operational Journey cluster: onboarding, dashboard, and KYC-heavy lifecycle flow, reconciling clarity with compliance requirements.
• Design system consolidation (your first mission): take the existing design system, analyze and diagnose it, consolidate and document it properly, and establish tokens and patterns the whole team can build on.
• Design standards across the domain: you set the quality bar and guide design decisions in areas without a dedicated designer yet, including the developer-experience surface, through standards and critique, not by producing every screen.
• Mentorship: you raise the craft of other designers on the team when needed.

How you will work

You report to the Product Design & UX Director for Customer Lifecycle. You are the senior design owner in the domain at the outset, setting standards, shipping craft, and building the system others rely on. Your time splits between product work and system consolidation, weighted toward the system early while the foundation is built, then rebalancing toward product. The domain works from validated findings rather than assumptions and values direct, candid critique.

What we're looking for

In priority order:

• Product design craft, first and foremost. An excellent product designer with a portfolio that shows depth, complex flows made genuinely simple, decisions grounded in user problems rather than decoration. This is the primary bar.
• Systems thinking you can demonstrate. You have built reusable components, tokens, and patterns with rigor, thinking about consistency, versioning, and how others will use what you make. You need not have single-handedly rebuilt a legacy system, but you should show the instinct and the mechanics.
• Fluency with the discipline of disclosure. In regulated products, design is often the instrument of compliance, communicating required information so users genuinely understand it. Experience with this kind of high-stakes clarity is a strong signal.

A strong plus: consolidating or migrating an existing design system; fintech or payments product design; front-end literacy; a track record of mentoring designers up.

Responsibilities :

• Shall act as the Company's focal point for the development and implementation of the Port Facility Security Management System in coordination with the appointed Recognized Security Organization (RSO).
• Lead and coordinate the preparation of the Port Facility Security Assessment (PFSA).
• Review and validate PFSA findings, security risks, and recommended mitigation measures proposed by the RSO.
• Coordinate the development, review, and finalization of the Port Facility Security Plan (PFSP).
• Ensure PFSP is practical, operationally effective, and aligned with terminal operations.
• Coordinate security gap assessments during engineering, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness phases.
• Monitor RSO project progress, deliverables, schedules, and quality of work.
• Review technical reports, drawings, and recommendations submitted by the RSO.
• Coordinate multidisciplinary meetings involving Marine Operations, Security, HSE, Engineering, Operations, and Project teams during PFSA/PFSP development.
• Ensure all security measures recommended by the RSO are technically feasible and incorporated into facility design and operational procedures.
• Coordinate implementation of corrective actions arising from PFSA recommendations.
• Support budget preparation for ISPS implementation, including security infrastructure, systems, equipment, training, and manpower.
• Coordinate pre-verification activities prior to regulatory inspections.
• Facilitate verification by the Directorate General of Sea Transportation and other competent authorities for Statement of Compliance of a Port Facility (SoCPF).
• Coordinate closure of findings raised during verification and certification processes.
• Maintain communication with the RSO throughout the project lifecycle and ensure timely completion of all contractual deliverables.

Qualification :

• Minimum Bachelor Degree in one of the following disciplines: Marine Transportation, Nautical Science, Marine Engineering, Maritime Studies, and all Engineering disciplines.
• Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in Port Operation (TUKS or Tersus)
• Mandatory Certified Port Facility Security Officer (PFSO) IMO Model Course 3.21
• Have expert knowledge about vessel operations, as well as the associated Port operations.
• Good English communication skills, spoken and written.
• Proficient in Microsoft Office

This position will be placed at Site Office Cilegon
